title: AI-assisted RapiD mapping in HOT's February 2023 Türkiye earthquake activation was up to 12.4% slower and was disabled; OSM data still reached AKUT and AFAD
summary: OSM wiki: University of Colorado Boulder/Indiana University research found RapiD AI-assisted contributors up to 12.4% slower; RapiD disabled; OSM data used by AKUT and AFAD. No AI benefit documented.
account: After the M7.8 earthquake in Türkiye on 6 February 2023, the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) activated, led by the Turkish community Yer Çizenler, with Tasking Manager projects for roads and buildings in Türkiye and Syria. The OpenStreetMap wiki page for the response (community-authored, last modified 5 June 2026) states that, because of the large project areas, AI-assisted mapping with the RapiD editor was originally encouraged but turned out to be counter-productive and was then disabled: research from the University of Colorado Boulder and Indiana University, shared with HOT in August 2023 and comparing 1,650 Tasking Manager contributors before and during the response, found contributors using RapiD mapped tasks up to 12.4% slower than those not using AI-assisted mapping, and validators reported many data-quality issues from RapiD contributors, which led to RapiD being disabled on all activation projects. The same page records that OSM data supported rescue coordination by the AKUT Search and Rescue Association and AFAD, public-health programming in the Kahramanmaraş tent city, and the World Bank's GRADE damage report. HOT's own activation and size-up pages (Internet Archive captures of 7 February and 29 May 2023) mention no AI tool and list no partner requests. No source on file documents Microsoft building footprints, HOT's fAIr or Meta maps in this response, nor any AI role in HOT's 2022 Pakistan floods activation; Cyclone Idai material was not found.
purpose: AI-assisted mapping was encouraged to speed building and road mapping over large areas for responders; the read evidence shows it slowed mapping and lowered quality in this activation, so the claimed benefit was not delivered.
system: RapiD editor (AI-assisted mapping) used on HOT Tasking Manager projects; the sources do not name its developer
deployer: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team with Yer Çizenler (activation lead)
taxonomy_note: The claimed good was faster mapping per contributor; the only independent study found contributors up to 12.4% slower and the tool was disabled.

ratings.reason: No AI-attributable outcome: the AI-assisted editor was found slower and was disabled.
No AI-attributable outcome: responders' use of OSM data is documented, but not tied to AI-derived features; the AI tool reduced mapping speed.

ai_role.statement: The AI component (RapiD AI-assisted mapping) is documented by the community-authored OSM wiki as counter-productive: up to 12.4% slower task mapping and validator-reported quality problems, after which it was disabled on all activation projects. Use of OSM data by AKUT, AFAD, a tent-city health team and the World Bank is documented on the same page but is not attributed to AI-derived data. HOT's activation and size-up pages, read from the Internet Archive, contain no AI mention. No source on file documents Microsoft building footprints, fAIr or Meta maps in the 2023 Türkiye, 2022 Pakistan or 2019 Idai responses.
